bull.b: Sequential EBITDA improvement and lower operating expenses indicate that cost actions are beginning to improve operating leverage. If sustained, these measures can reduce the revenue scale required to reach management’s profitability target.

The Dakota Lithium acquisition and heavy-duty trucking pipeline broaden exposure beyond the soft RV market. Additional brands, channels, and fleet deployments could create more diversified revenue and improve capacity utilization over time.

Patent protection for dry-electrode and solid-state processes may strengthen differentiation, support future product development, and improve partnership prospects. These technologies could become strategic assets if commercialization delivers safer or lower-cost storage.

bear.b: Large operating losses and deeply negative cash flow show that the business is not self-funding. Continued burn may require additional financing, constrain investment in growth initiatives, and increase dependence on favorable lender or capital-market access.

Declining revenue and continued dependence on RV-related demand expose Dragonfly to a weak end market. The modest Q3 sales outlook suggests that new trucking and specialty-market growth has not yet offset pressure in the core business.

Covenant concessions provide liquidity but signal financial strain and may increase future interest obligations. At the same time, the tariff refund means reported margin expansion was partly non-recurring, limiting confidence in underlying profitability.
